rationale:
Positives: The agent authenticated the user correctly using full name + zip. It acted only on the user’s own orders. It verified order statuses before changes (address change on pending #W6729841, item modification on pending #W4219264, and an exchange on delivered #W3445693). Product and pricing details were consistent with tool outputs (watch variant change led to a $121.20 refund; air purifier exchange showed a $24.24 upcharge). The watch modification was properly confirmed before executing. 

Failures: The agent executed order-changing writes without prior explicit confirmation in two cases: (1) It updated the shipping address for order #W6729841 immediately after the user identified the source order, without restating the exact change and obtaining explicit confirmation per policy. (2) It submitted the exchange for the delivered air purifier on #W3445693 without first stating the exact exchange details and getting the user’s explicit approval. Additionally, it stated that an email with return instructions would be sent, which was not explicitly supported by tool outputs, risking unsupported information. These issues violate the requirement to confirm before any order-changing action and to avoid inventing details. 

Given these policy violations, the conversation does not meet the pass bar.
